title: The 11 and 13 chords
summary: The last two extensions, and why players leave notes out.

steps.title: 11 chord
steps.body:
The 11th is the 4th counted from the octave above. An **11 chord** is a 7th chord with the 9th and 11th added. In practice players leave out the 3rd, which clashes with the 11th: a common C11 is C, G, B♭, D and F.

**Why it matters:** It is the open, gospel and fusion sound, a bit like a 7sus4 with extra colour.

steps.title: 13 chord
steps.body:
The 13th is the 6th counted from the octave above. A **13 chord** is a dominant 7th chord with the 13th added. Players usually keep just the root, 3rd, 7th and 13th: C13 is C, E, B♭ and A.

**Why it matters:** It is the rich, bluesy dominant chord of jazz and soul. Many players use G13 in place of G7.

steps.title: Leaving notes out
steps.body: With seven notes you would need three hands, so players keep the notes that give the chord its colour.

items.prompt: Play C, E, Bb and A together: a C13.
Play C, G, Bb, D and F together: a C11.

steps.title: Colour a 7th
steps.body: Play C7, then move the G up a whole step to A: that is a C13. Hear how much richer it is.

items.prompt: Play G, B, F and E together: a G13.
Which note is the 3rd of this chord?
